resolved.question: Should the advisor's cohort-pass-before-advance rule (advisor-orchestrator.md 'Stage-shape orchestration') accommodate plans that intentionally produce intermediate validate-pending fails — or should plans avoid that pattern?

(B) Amend the planner template to forbid intentional-fail cohort patterns — plans must order tasks so each cohort barrier is independently green-able

resolved.question: How does an impl-task Junior worktree commit onto phase-v1-JM-d when create_task only takes a description and the daemon's base is governance-v0? bm-cut #8 created phase-v1-JM-d on the EliteDesk's main checkout but the MCP exposes no base-branch override; future impl tasks will branch off governance-v0 and finalize back to it.
options: (A) Push phase-v1-JM-d to origin from inside the bm-cut subagent so it's a remote ref; teach impl-task subagent to git fetch + checkout phase-v1-JM-d at task start (ignoring its junior/role-* worktree branch as a transport vehicle), commit there, then push the phase branch directly. Junior's finalize-merge-to-base becomes a no-op because the worktree branch has no commits. Contradicts bm-cut Phase 3 'don't push until first impl commit' but the deferral was specifically to avoid empty-branch PR-target confusion — that risk lapses the moment task 1 is queued.

(B) Add base_branch override to the junior-brehon MCP create_task tool + Junior daemon (.junior/config.yaml or per-task field). Set it to phase-v1-JM-d after bm-cut. Each impl-task worktree branches off phase-v1-JM-d, finalize merges back to phase-v1-JM-d. Cleanest semantics but requires shipping MCP/daemon code.

(C) bm-cut subagent should reconfigure the daemon's base in-place after cutting (e.g. yq write into .junior/config.yaml + restart the daemon). bm-merge later resets it to governance-v0. Cheap if the daemon honors config reloads but adds restart-during-task fragility and breaks the abstraction that bm-task verbs are read-only on infra.

(D) Skip the phase-branch model entirely for v1-JM-d: queue impl tasks against governance-v0, accept that finalize lands them on trunk, do bm-pr from governance-v0 directly. Loses CR-on-PR review of the phase-as-unit but gets us moving. Departs from the established v0/v1 phase-branch convention.
resolved.context: After bm-cut #8 (commit 9abe25a) the EliteDesk has phase-v1-JM-d as a local branch ahead of governance-v0 by one commit (the runlog). The branch is not on origin (per bm-cut Phase 3). Junior's create_task MCP only accepts {description}; .junior/config.yaml has no base_branch field. The advisor-orchestrator stage map says 'bm-cut complete → queue impl-task for plan task 1' but doesn't specify how the impl task lands on phase-v1-JM-d. Per feedback_pr_per_phase.md code deliveries run on phase branch + PR — that contract assumes the phase branch is reachable by impl tasks. Without resolution, queueing impl-task #1 will likely commit to governance-v0 and pollute trunk.
resolved.answer:
(B) baseBranch override via .junior/config.yaml. Smallest slice: (1) add `base_branch:` field to .junior/config.yaml read at daemon start, default governance-v0; (2) extend bm-cut Phase 6 to write `base_branch: phase-<suffix>` after cutting + `systemctl reload junior@brehon-fork` (restart if reload unsupported); (3) extend bm-merge to reset to governance-v0 after merge; (4) no create_task MCP API change — MCP shells to junior CLI which reads config. Rationale: only option where the orchestrator stage map abstraction matches reality; one-time investment reused every sub-phase; removes silent-trunk-pollution bug class entirely. (A) was second-best but loads correctness onto subagent-rule discipline; (C) restarts daemon mid-orchestration and crosses bm-read-only-on-infra; (D) abandons phase-branch contract. Implementation queued as a chore impl-task before JM-d task 1.

ADDENDUM 2026-04-27 (post-source-investigation): the slice reduces from a 4-step daemon-code change to a 1-step git checkout. Junior's CLI `task add` (src/cli/task.ts:40) sets `baseBranch = await getCurrentBranch(repoPath)` at task-creation time, persisting per-job in the DB. The MCP `create_task` shells `junior task add <description>` over SSH. Therefore: (1) `ssh homeserver 'cd /srv/brehon-fork && git fetch origin && git checkout phase-v1-JM-d'` activates the phase branch as default base; (2) all subsequent MCP create_task calls inherit baseBranch=phase-v1-JM-d; (3) finalize merges each impl-task worktree into phase-v1-JM-d (executor.ts:390); (4) at bm-merge time, switch the main checkout back to governance-v0. No daemon source changes, no config schema extension, no MCP tool extension. Tradeoff: the main-checkout branch becomes a load-bearing piece of phase orchestration state — bm-cut should `git checkout` the phase branch on the main checkout (not just inside its worktree), and bm-merge should `git checkout governance-v0`. This is a smaller change to the bm-cut/bm-merge scripts, not the daemon. Original (B) plan abandoned in favour of this discovery.

resolved.question: Layer C concurrency model: cargo runs against committed code. Two main options to avoid contention with a running impl-task on the same worktree: (a) tmp-dir clone — git clone phase-branch into /tmp/validate-<sha>/ each run, run cargo there; (b) worktree-reuse — cargo runs in the existing phase-branch worktree, blocked by flock if impl-task is editing.
options: (a) tmp-dir clone — robust, cold cargo cache per run
(b) worktree-reuse with flock — fast, risk of file conflicts
(c) Hybrid: tmp-dir for first run, worktree-reuse for retries
(d) Shared target dir + tmp-dir source
resolved.context: Source: validate-agent-design.md §9.2(4) + §8 'Failure modes to design against'. Judgment-heavy — affects validate-runner's robustness model + cold-cache cost per validation. Brief recommends option (a). Cargo cache penalty is one-time per phase since /tmp/validate-* dirs persist within a sub-phase (validate-runner can keep CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/validate-<phase>/target/ as a phase-scoped shared cache, deleting only on phase close). Worktree-reuse fails when an impl-task pre-commit edit overlaps validate's read.
resolved.answer: (a) tmp-dir clone (per user 2026-04-27). Each validate run does `git clone --shared --branch <commit_sha> /tmp/validate-<sha>/`, sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/validate-<phase>/target/ (shared across runs within a phase to keep cargo cache warm), runs cargo there, deletes the source dir after (target dir persists until phase close). Robust: zero risk of clobbering an in-flight impl-task. The cargo cache penalty is mitigated by phase-scoped target dir reuse — cold cache only on first validation per phase. Reasoning supplemental to user choice: option (d) shared target dir was rejected because cargo's incremental compilation state isn't robust under concurrent writes. Option (b) flock has a hidden failure mode where validate queues indefinitely behind a stuck impl-task. Option (c) hybrid adds run-mode logic to validate-runner unnecessarily.

resolved.question: Empirical probe of `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` on gh CLI 2.89.0 against three real workflow-run scenarios revealed it returns exit 0 for ALL three: (a) already-completed-success run (25017407689), (b) already-completed-failure run (25017407659), (c) in-progress run watched live to completion-failure (25017554049). options: (a) ci-watcher must NEVER trust --exit-status; instead always run `gh run view <id> --json conclusion --jq '.conclusion'` post-watch and branch on the conclusion string (success | failure | cancelled | timed_out | etc)

resolved.context: Three probes captured during v1-validate-agent Task 2 empirical-gating. The defensive fallback in plan §10.6 — 'post-watch gh run view to disambiguate' — was framed as defensive; empirical evidence makes it MANDATORY. ci-watcher's exit-code table is therefore: 'exit code from gh run watch is unreliable; always disambiguate via gh run view conclusion'. resolved.answer: (a) — ci-watcher MUST always run `gh run view <id> --json conclusion --jq '.conclusion'` after `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` returns; classify on the conclusion string, never on the exit code. Cancelled and queued-only probes deferred — not blocking ci-watcher authoring because the conclusion-string fallback covers all conclusion values (success | failure | cancelled | timed_out | action_required | neutral | skipped | stale).

resolved.answer: Option (A) — cascade.
